topicTitle: Native Web Components & Shadow DOM Encapsulation

lessons.title: Custom Elements API & Lifecycle Callback Handlers
lessons.description: Create reusable HTML elements with custom behavior using the Custom Elements API.

sections.heading: What are Custom Elements?
paragraphs: Custom Elements let you define new HTML tags with their own behavior. They follow the same lifecycle as built-in elements: creation, connection, updates and disconnection.
list: Extends HTMLElement to get full DOM element capabilities

codeExamples.heading: Custom element with lifecycle
explanation: Extend HTMLElement to create a custom element class.
Constructor sets up the shadow DOM and initial state.
connectedCallback runs when the element is added to the page.

practice.task: Create a custom <my-clock> element that displays the current time and updates every second.
hints: Use setInterval in connectedCallback, clearInterval in disconnectedCallback.
Display time in the shadow DOM.

keyTakeaways: Custom Elements let you create reusable HTML tags with custom behavior.
Lifecycle callbacks handle creation, connection and disconnection.
Custom element names must contain a hyphen.
They work with standard DOM APIs and frameworks.
lessons.challenge: Build a <my-tabs> custom element with tab switching and keyboard navigation.

lessons.title: DOM Encapsulation via Shadow DOM (open vs closed)
lessons.description: Shadow DOM isolates your component's internal DOM and styles from the rest of the page.

sections.heading: Shadow DOM basics
list: this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" }) — external code can access the shadow root
Styles inside shadow DOM don't leak out — complete isolation
External styles don't affect the shadow DOM

codeExamples.heading: Shadow DOM style isolation
explanation: Shadow DOM creates an isolated DOM tree inside your component.
CSS inside the shadow root doesn't affect or get affected by the outside page.
slot elements project external content into the shadow DOM.
This gives you true style encapsulation — no CSS conflicts.

practice.task: Create a <my-button> component with Shadow DOM that has its own styles, unaffected by external CSS.
hints: Define styles inside the shadow root.
Test by adding conflicting global CSS — the component should be unaffected.

keyTakeaways: Shadow DOM isolates a component's DOM and styles from the page.
open mode lets external code access the shadow root; closed hides it.
slot elements project external content into the shadow DOM.
Shadow DOM provides true style encapsulation — no CSS conflicts.
lessons.challenge: Build a complete UI component library using Shadow DOM with a button, input, card and modal.

lessons.title: Reusable UI Components using <template> & <slot> Elements
lessons.description: HTML templates and slots let you define reusable component structures with customizable content areas.

sections.heading: Templates and slots
list: <template> — defines reusable HTML that isn't rendered until activated
<slot> — placeholder for external content in Shadow DOM
<slot name="x"> — named slots for specific content areas
Default content appears when no slot content is provided

codeExamples.heading: Template and slot usage
explanation: Named slots let you project content to specific locations.
Default slot content appears when no matching slot is provided.
::slotted() styles projected content from outside the shadow DOM.
Templates and slots make components truly reusable.

practice.task: Build a <my-card> component with named slots for header, body and footer. Provide default content for each slot.
hints: Test with and without slot content to verify defaults work.
Style the card with Shadow DOM styles.

keyTakeaways: Templates define reusable HTML structures that aren't rendered until activated.
Slots project external content into specific locations in the shadow DOM.
Named slots target specific content areas; default slots handle the rest.
These APIs make Web Components truly reusable and composable.
lessons.challenge: Build a complete component library with a button, input, card and modal — all using slots for content projection.
